newsitem.title: INDIA: India's reforms seem to be slowing - IMF chief.
newsitem.headline: India's reforms seem to be slowing - IMF chief.

text.p: International Monetary Fund managing director Michel Camdessus said on Wednesday that a slowdown in Indian trade seemed to indicate that the nation's economic reform programme was losing some momentum.
"It appears that the first wave of structural measures is losing a little bit of momentum as is shown by figures this year in trade," Camdessus told a news conference in the Indian capital.
India's exports between April 1996 and January 1997 grew by 6.19 percent compared with the same period one year earlier.
That was well below the 22 percent exports growth rate between April 1995 and January 1996 compared with the same 10-month period one year earlier.
Camdessus, on the last day of a four-day visit to India, recommended a "bolder strategy" of reform in which New Delhi would pursue budget consolidation and public sector changes.
The IMF chief called for a "second wave of structural reforms" to help propel the Indian economy forward.
